security_subject_or_principal.implementation_summary: Identifies X509Certificate methods whose attributes (subject/SAN/serial) represent the holder's certificate used for authentication.

protected_target_or_security_object.implementation_summary: Targets calls that establish or set an authenticated identity/session (authenticate/login/createSession/etc.).

attacker_controlled_input_or_trigger.implementation_summary: Treats certificate-derived attributes (subject/SAN/serial or X500Principal.getName) as externally supplied identity keys used to trigger authentication mapping.

decisive_security_relation.implementation_summary: Encodes the too-permissive mapping where certificate attributes are directly used as the identity argument in authentication/session-establishing calls.

required_validation_or_authorization_con.implementation_summary: Requires absence of validation/scoping in the same scope (e.g., verify/validate/check or EKU/KeyUsage/issuer/basic constraints checks) before mapping certificate attributes to identity.

security_sensitive_effect.implementation_summary: Reports the certificate-derived identity reaching an authentication sink, implying potential abuse of authenticated access beyond intended scope.
